missions.tainan_title: Rights and Land Under Japanese Rule: Historical Restoration Mission
missions.tainan_description: Become a grassroots civil servant of the Governor-General's Office and explore how Japan established a high-pressure and fiscally self-sufficient colonial rule through law, police systems, and financial means.
missions.tainan_main_goal: Understand how the Japanese government established a high-pressure and fiscally self-sufficient colonial system in a short period through legal and economic means, and master its colonial philosophy.
missions.tainan_player_role: Grassroots Civil Servant of Taiwan Governor-General's Office
missions.tainan_player_backstory: You were just assigned to Taiwan in 1905 to assist with civil affairs in the Tainan area. Although your rank is not high, you are well aware that the power of the Governor-General's Office comes from 'Law No. 63'. Your task is to ensure that the colonial system operates smoothly and maintain stable finances to achieve the goal of the colony being self-supporting.
missions.stage_1_desc: You just arrived in Tainan City, one of the power centers of the early colonial period. You see your colleague, Japanese police officer Satō, lecturing several Taiwanese civilians.
missions.stage_1_question: Please ask NPCs to understand how the colonial government obtained absolute political power.
missions.stage_1_hint: Police Officer Satō should know best about the implementation of law and power. You can start by asking him what 'Law No. 63' is.
missions.stage_1_completion: You have mastered the legal foundation of rule. But to understand the policies deeply, you need to know the philosophy and repressive measures behind them.
missions.stage_2_title: Stage 2: Governing Philosophy and Repressive Measures
missions.stage_2_desc: You have understood the legal foundation of the Governor-General's Office. Now, explore the governing philosophy behind these systems and the harsh measures used to suppress early resistance.
missions.stage_2_question: What was the government's governing philosophy in the early colonial period? And what was the most severe law they used to suppress rebellion?
missions.stage_2_completion: You successfully understood Gotō Shinpei's biological principle and the Bandit Punishment Ordinance. This laid the foundation for implementing grassroots control and moving to the next task.
missions.stage_3_desc: Now you must figure out how this power was exercised to the most basic levels of Taiwanese society.
missions.stage_3_question: Besides the central Governor-General's Office, what methods did they use to control the most basic levels of Taiwanese society?
missions.stage_3_completion: You successfully understood grassroots control measures. But executing these tight controls requires enormous funds. Now, find out how the government raised the necessary money.
missions.stage_4_desc: You have already mastered the political control measures. Your second task is to clarify the financial foundation of the colonial government. The colony must be self-supporting, and land survey and monopoly systems are key clues.
missions.stage_4_question: How were the government's main financial sources established in the early colonial period? (Hint: requires two main means)
missions.stage_4_hint: Land surveyor Yamamoto is responsible for measurement and taxation. Police officer Satō is responsible for monopoly enforcement. You need to ask both to get complete financial clues.
missions.stage_4_completion: Excellent! You have understood the colony's main sources of revenue.
missions.stage_5_desc: You have understood the colony's main sources of revenue. Now, investigate what infrastructure the government used these funds for to benefit both rule and modernization.
missions.stage_5_question: Please ask NPCs what important financial and transportation infrastructure the Governor-General's Office built.
missions.stage_5_completion: Congratulations! You have mastered all the core information about the political, social control, financial, and infrastructure foundations of the colonial system. You can now start writing your summary report.
missions.stage_6_desc: You have completed all investigations. Now you need to submit a concise report to the Governor-General's Office summarizing your understanding of the foundations of colonial rule.
missions.stage_6_question: Please use three core policies or systems (law, social control, finance) to summarize the establishment process of the colonial system during this period.
missions.stage_6_completion: Mission complete! You have gained a comprehensive understanding of how the colonial system was established in the early Japanese period.
missions.learning_goal_1: Understand the absolute power granted to the Governor by 'Law No. 63'
missions.learning_goal_2: Recognize Gotō Shinpei's 'biological principle' governing philosophy
missions.learning_goal_3: Understand how police politics and the baojia system controlled grassroots society
missions.learning_goal_4: Master how land surveys and monopoly systems established the financial foundation
missions.learning_goal_5: Recognize modernization infrastructure in the early Japanese period
missions.learning_goal_6: Comprehensively evaluate the dual characteristics of 'colonization' and 'modernization' in colonial rule

s1.title: Historical Dialogue System
s1.subtitle: Archive Repair V2.2
s1.memory_gaps_desc: The archives are unclear due to age. Please use interviews to reconstruct the scene details of that time.
s1.identity_desc: Mr. Suzuki, belonging to a local civil servant of the Taiwan Governor-General's Office, unlike the police carrying batons or surveyors operating instruments, you are responsible for implementing civil affairs and keeping records.
s1.law_system_hint: The special legal system established by Japan in Taiwan
s1.executing_body_hint: The grassroots responsible for implementing policies

s2.title: Select Investigation Target
s2.police_officer_desc: A Japanese police officer responsible for executing Governor-General's Office orders. Powerful and commands respect.
s2.student_desc: A public school student in Tainan City who can provide perspective on the life of grassroots Taiwanese people.
s2.land_surveyor_desc: A surveyor responsible for land surveys and forestry investigations. Knowledgeable about financial and land information.
